segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Good evening everyone.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: My name’s Phil Sutton, and I’m chairman of the Highways Committee.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’ve called this meeting to inform members of the public about the new regulations for traffic and parking we’re proposing for Granford.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: I’ll start by summarising these changes before we open the meeting to questions.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So, why do we need to make these changes to traffic systems in Granford?

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Well, we’re very aware that traffic is becoming an increasing problem.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s been especially noticeable with the increase in heavy traffic while they’ve been building the new hospital.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But it’s the overall rise in the volume of traffic of all kinds that’s concerning us.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: To date there’s not been any increase in traffic accidents, but that’s not something we want to see happen, obviously.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We recently carried out a survey of local residents, and their responses were interesting.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: People were very concerned about the lack of visibility on some roads due to cars parked along the sides of the roads.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’d expected complaints about the congestion near the school when parents are dropping off their children or picking them up, but this wasn’t top of the list, and nor were noise and fumes from trucks and lorries, though they were mentioned by some people.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We think these new traffic regulations would make a lot of difference.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But we still have a long way to go.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’ve managed to keep our proposals within budget, just, so they can be covered by the Council.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: But, of course, it’s no good introducing new regulations if we don’t have a way of making sure that everyone obeys them, and that’s an area we’re still working on with the help of representatives from the police force. —————– OK, so this slide shows a map of the central area of Granford, with the High Street in the middle and School Road on the right.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Now, we already have a set of traffic lights in the High Street at the junction with Station Road, but we’re planning to have another set at the other end, at the School Road junction, to regulate the flow or traffic along the High Street.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’re decided we definitely need a pedestrian crossing.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We considered putting this on School Road, just outside the school, but in the end we decided that could lead to a lot of traffic congestion so we decided to locate it on the High Street, crossing the road in front of the supermarket.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: That’s a very busy area, so it should help things there.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We’re proposing some changes to parking.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: At present, parking isn’t allowed on the High Street outside the library, but we’re going to change that, and allow parking there, but not at the other end of the High Street near School Road.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: There’ll be a new ‘No Parking’ sign on School Road, just by the entrance to the school, forbidding parking for 25 metres.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: This should improve visibility for drivers and pedestrians, especially on the bend just to the north of the school.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: As far as disabled drivers are concerned, at present they have parking outside the supermarket, but lorries also use those spaces, so we’ve got two new disabled parking spaces on the side road up towards the bank.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: It’s not ideal, but probably better than the present arrangement.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We also plan to widen the pavement on School Road.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: We think we can manage to get an extra half-metre on the bend just before you get to the school, on the same side of the road.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: Finally, we’ve introduced new restrictions on loading and unloading for the supermarket, so lorries will only be allowed to stop there before 8 am.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: That’s the supermarket on School Road – we kept to the existing arrangements with the High Street supermarket.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: OK.

segments.speaker: SPEAKER
segments.en: So that’s about it.
